name: Vanguardism
summary: Vanguardism holds that the working class, left to itself, develops only trade-union consciousness, and that a disciplined party of committed, mostly professional revolutionaries must bring it political consciousness and lead it to overthrow capitalism and establish proletarian rule. It is the Leninist theory of the party, set out in What Is to Be Done? and tied to iron party discipline under democratic centralism. The theory concerns how the revolutionary party is built and led; its defining sources state few positions beyond that.
scope: The Leninist theory of the vanguard party as defined by the Verso encyclopedia entry (Georgakas), Britannica's article on Leninism, Blackledge's review of Lih and Mandel's essay, and as set out in Lenin's What Is to Be Done? (1902), the text those sources name. It does not cover Leninism's other doctrines (see leninism and marxism-leninism), the regimes that ruled under it, or later Trotskyist, Maoist or Third World vanguardisms. Earlier answers drawn from Wikipedia's summary or from the communist-state setting were nulled in the 2026-11-17 pass.

notes: Themes searched: party organisation, discipline and factions, membership, secrecy and professionalism, trade unions, parliaments and elections, reform versus revolution, the dictatorship of the proletariat, class alliances, in Lenin's party texts (What Is to Be Done?, One Step Forward, Two Steps Back, 'Left-Wing' Communism) and the defining reference works. Only What Is to Be Done? is named often enough by the defining sources to count as the theory's own text, so the later Lenin texts (read, saved locally) answer nothing here. The sources hold nothing on most statements (economy, society, culture, ecology, technology, immigration, justice, foreign policy): the concept concerns how the revolutionary party is built and led, and the many nulls are the honest result. Lenin never used the term 'vanguard party' himself (Wikipedia, citing Geier, attributes it to Zinoviev).
